title: Unbind BrCliBeadStore from the bf binary — its argv is correct beads_rust, discover() resolves bf first
description:
src/bead_store/mod.rs:1550-1563 builds `create --title T --body B --json --silent [--labels a,b]`. bf 0.4.1 create accepts NONE of --body, --silent, --labels — only --title --description --type --priority --assignee --label (repeated) --json --envelope --no-auto-flush --no-progress --workspace. Verified via `bf create --help` on 2026-08-11.

BrCliBeadStore is the store EVERY worker path uses (worker/mod.rs:1385, supervisor/mod.rs:214, strand/explore.rs:71/:450, strand/splice.rs:747/:839/:999) and its discover() resolves `bf` FIRST — so the fleet runs the old br dialect against a binary that rejects it. BfCliBeadStore::create_bead (:2267-2280) already does it correctly but is only constructed in cli/mod.rs:997/:3384.

Blast radius: create_bead fails with a clap parse error (exit 2), and through the trait default split_bead (:646-668) that takes ALL mitosis child creation with it.

Deliverables:
- BrCliBeadStore::create_bead emits `--description` and repeated `--label`, matching BfCliBeadStore.
- Drop --json/--silent; bf create prints the bare ID on stdout already (the existing stdout.trim() parse is correct).
- A fixture-CLI test asserting the exact argv, so this cannot regress silently.

Acceptance criteria:
- Argv assertion test passes for create_bead with 0, 1, and 2 labels.
- fmt + clippy + full test suite green on iad-ci.
- Sequenced BEFORE the bead_store module split so the two do not collide in the same file.

See docs/adr/013-pluggable-bead-cli-backends.md, Addendum.
close_reason: Fixed BrCliBeadStore::create_bead to use bf 0.4.1+ CLI dialect (--description, repeated --label) instead of legacy br dialect (--body, --silent, comma-separated --labels). Also fixed add_dependency to use --blocks instead of --type blocks. All argv assertion tests pass (0, 1, 2, 3 labels), fmt + clippy green, commit a9d3e11 pushed to main.

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-11 — THE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION PRESCRIBES THE WRONG FIX. DO NOT rewrite --body to --description in this store.

The real beads_rust binary is ~/.cargo/bin/br v0.1.28 (dicklesworthstone/beads_rust). ~/.local/bin/br is a SHIM that execs bf, so `which br` does not find it — which is how this went unnoticed.

Probed against real br 0.1.28:
- create -d/--description [aliases: --body] — --body IS VALID
- --silent — VALID
- -l/--labels comma-separated — VALID
- dep add <ISSUE> <DEPENDS_ON> -t blocks — TWO positionals, VALID

So BrCliBeadStore::create_bead (:1550-1563) and add_dependency (:1579) are CORRECT beads_rust. Nothing about their argv is stale.

The actual defect is BrCliBeadStore::discover (:758-775): it resolves bf BEFORE br, binding the beads_rust adapter to the bead-forge binary, which rejects that argv. Compounding it, bf-only calls were grafted into this store — claim (:1428-1437), release (:1479-1486), split (:1485/:1508) via bf batch, and claim_auto via bf claim (:1194-1220) — using the second resolver at :1127. beads_rust has NEITHER subcommand.

REVISED DELIVERABLES:
- Do NOT touch create_bead or add_dependency argv in this store.
- Make BrCliBeadStore resolve br only, and confirm it is real beads_rust, not the shim (the shim execs bf and will silently pass a --version check).
- Remove the grafted bf batch/claim paths and the :1127 resolver from this store; claim/release/clear_assignee use update -s <status> --assignee ..., which beads_rust has.
- claim_auto: beads_rust has no claim subcommand — implement as non-atomic ready then claim(id), and LOG the downgrade (real TOCTOU window, matters for multi-worker fleets).
- Argv assertion tests pinned to real br 0.1.28 help output.

The one genuine argv bug is in the OTHER store: BfCliBeadStore::add_dependency (:2288) sends two positionals; bf 0.4.1 takes one (<BLOCKER> --blocks <BLOCKED>). Tracked on bf-s5hb8, now narrowed to the bf store only.

See docs/adr/013-pluggable-bead-cli-backends.md section 5 and Revision History.

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
SCOPE NOTE 2026-08-11 (ADR-013 draft 3) — this bead survives as the INTERIM tactical fix. Keep it narrow.

The final design deletes BrCliBeadStore entirely and replaces both stores with one descriptor-driven CliBeadStore (bf-1awps). That work is ~6 beads deep and gated behind the descriptor type, the strategy set, and the engine. Meanwhile the chimera is breaking mitosis child creation on every fleet host TODAY.

title: Verify NEEDLE OTLP telemetry emits correctly end-to-end (post-crash-fix)
description:
## Purpose

bf-4icyq fixes the startup crash so a worker with `otlp_sink.enabled: true`
can boot at all. That only proves it doesn't crash — it does not prove the
telemetry it emits is correct, complete, or actually reaches any consumer.
This bead is the follow-on: verify the signal itself, end-to-end, across
every hop and every consumer.

Blocked on bf-4icyq (can't meaningfully test emission until the worker can
stay up).

## What NEEDLE actually emits (confirmed by reading src/telemetry/otlp.rs)

- **Logs**: `emit_log()` fires for every single TelemetryEvent, unconditionally
  — attributes `event_type`, `worker_id`, `session_id`, `sequence`, optional
  `bead_id`, JSON-string body. This is the complete event stream.
- **Metrics**: only specific event types map to instruments (see
  `dispatch_event`'s match arms). Confirmed instrument names as currently
  implemented: `needle.workers.active`, `needle.beads.claimed`,
  `needle.beads.completed`, `needle.beads.duration`, `needle.claim.attempts`,
  `needle.strand.duration`, `needle.agent.duration`,
  `needle.agent.tokens.input`, `needle.agent.tokens.output`,
  `needle.cost.usd`, `needle.heartbeat.age`, `needle.queue.depth`,
  `needle.peers.stale`, `needle.mitosis.children_created`. Export cadence is
  `PeriodicReader` on `config.telemetry.otlp_sink.metrics_interval_secs`
  (10s in ex44's current config).
- **Traces**: a tracer/span pipeline exists (`build_grpc_providers` /
  `build_http_providers` both construct a `SdkTracerProvider`), but
  `dispatch_event` only explicitly emits span *events* for
  `heartbeat.emitted`/`build.heartbeat` via `emit_span_event`. Confirm during
  testing whether any real spans (not just span events) are actually
  produced, since the doc comment above `dispatch_event` claims several
  event types map to spans but the match arms mostly only touch metrics/logs.

**Known naming discrepancy to check**: FABRIC's own docs
(`FABRIC/docs/needle-exporter-wiring.md`) describe NEEDLE emitting
`needle.worker.tokens.in`, `needle.worker.tokens.out`, `needle.worker.cost.usd`,
`needle.worker.beads.completed/failed`, `needle.worker.errors`,
`needle.bead.duration` — this does **not** match the instrument names
actually in `otlp.rs` today (listed above). Either FABRIC's doc is stale
against an older NEEDLE version, or there's a real mismatch that would
silently break FABRIC's `INSTRUMENT_ALIASES` resolution and any Grafana
dashboard built against the documented names. Resolve which is true before
building anything downstream that depends on specific metric names.

## Test plan

### 1. Synthetic collector smoke test (no NEEDLE involved — isolates the collector/auth path)

```bash
curl -X POST http://needle-otel-ex44-apexalgo-iad-ts.ardenone.com:4318/v1/logs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EX44_OTLP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"resourceLogs":[{"resource":{"attributes":[{"key":"service.name","value":{"stringValue":"needle"}}]},"scopeLogs":[{"scope":{"name":"needle"},"logRecords":[{"timeUnixNano":"<now-ns>","body":{"stringValue":"{}"},"attributes":[{"key":"event_type","value":{"stringValue":"test.smoke"}},{"key":"worker_id","value":{"stringValue":"smoke-test"}}]}]}]}]}'
```

Confirms auth + routing works before trusting anything from a real worker.
A 200 with empty body `{}` (or `{"partialSuccess":{}}`) is success.

### 2. Collector self-metrics (confirms the collector actually received + forwarded, independent of NEEDLE or downstream stores)

The collector exposes its own Prometheus metrics on `:8888`
(`needle-otel-collector.needle-observability.svc.cluster.local:8888/metrics`,
cluster-internal only). After step 1 and again after a real worker run, check:

- `otelcol_receiver_accepted_log_records{receiver="otlp/ex44"}` — increments
- `otelcol_receiver_accepted_metric_points{receiver="otlp/ex44"}` — increments once a worker emits metrics
- `otelcol_exporter_sent_log_records{exporter="otlphttp/victorialogs"}` and `{exporter="otlphttp/dashboard"}` — both should increment together; if only one does, the fan-out is broken for the other
- `otelcol_exporter_sent_metric_points{exporter="prometheusremotewrite"}` — will be 0/failing until the apex Prometheus disk-full issue (found 2026-08-08, separate from this bead) is resolved — do not treat that as an OTLP bug
- Watch for `otelcol_exporter_send_failed_*` counters on any exporter — nonzero means silent drops downstream of the collector

### 3. Real worker test on ex44 (after bf-4icyq lands and needle-stable is rebuilt/deployed)

```bash
# Launch with an explicit, clearly-labeled identifier so its telemetry is easy to find downstream
tmux new-session -d -s needle-claude-code-glm47-otel-verify \
  "NEEDLE_INNER=1 /home/coding/.needle/bin/needle-stable run --workspace /home/coding/NEEDLE --agent claude-code-glm47 --count 1 --identifier otel-verify --timeout 1200 2>> /home/coding/.needle/logs/needle-claude-code-glm47-otel-verify.stderr.log"
```

- Confirm the process stays up (no panic) — this is bf-4icyq's own criterion, re-checked here as a gate before continuing.
- `grep -i "otlp\|export failed" .needle/logs/needle-claude-code-glm47-otel-verify.stderr.log` — should show no `OTLP log export failed` / `OTLP tracing layer export failure` WARN lines. If present, that's the auth/token question from bf-4icyq's parent investigation resurfacing — capture the exact error text, it will say why (401 vs timeout vs TLS).
- Let it run long enough to emit at least one full cycle: a claim attempt, a heartbeat (30s interval per `health.heartbeat_interval_secs`), and ideally one full bead completion — each exercises a different instrument/log path.

### 4. Logs path — VictoriaLogs + dashboard.ardenone.com/needle

- Query VictoriaLogs directly for the `otel-verify` worker's stream and confirm records with `event_type`/`worker_id`/`bead_id` attributes are present and match what the worker actually did (cross-check a few against the raw JSONL in `~/.needle/logs/` for the same worker — same events should appear in both, this is the dual-ingestion path FABRIC's doc describes).
- Hit `https://dashboard.ardenone.com/needle/api/dashboard` (authenticated) and confirm:
  - `environments.ex44.active_workers` reflects the new worker while it's active
  - `workers[]` contains an entry with `worker_id` containing `otel-verify`, correct `state`, and `last_seen` advancing
  - `events[]` contains real event types, not just heartbeats
- Open the actual page and confirm the SSE `/stream` pushes updates live (not just on manual reload) — watch the `#connection` badge go to "Live", and watch a row update in real time when the worker transitions state.

### 5. Metrics path — apex Prometheus / Grafana (blocked until the disk-full Prometheus issue is separately fixed)

- Once Prometheus is healthy again, query for the actual instrument names confirmed in the "what NEEDLE emits" section above (not the FABRIC-doc names, unless step 0 above resolves the discrepancy in FABRIC's favor) — e.g. `needle_beads_claimed_total{deployment_cluster="ex44"}`.
- Confirm `deployment.cluster`/`telemetry.source`/`fleet.name` attributes were correctly overwritten by the collector's `resource/ex44` processor (README says client-supplied values for these three are not trusted — verify the enforcement actually happens, don't just assume the config does what the README says).
- Confirm `needle.worker.pool` (client-supplied, not overwritten) survived intact.

### 6. Cleanup

Stop the `otel-verify` worker (`tmux kill-session -t needle-claude-code-glm47-otel-verify`) once verification is complete — it's a diagnostic worker, not meant to run indefinitely.

## Acceptance criteria

- Synthetic smoke test (step 1) succeeds independent of any real worker.
- Collector self-metrics (step 2) confirm accept + forward counts increment for both the VictoriaLogs and dashboard exporters.
- A real worker (step 3) runs for at least one full bead lifecycle with zero `OTLP ... export failed` warnings in its own log.
- At least one real event from that worker is independently confirmed in VictoriaLogs, in the raw JSONL, AND on `dashboard.ardenone.com/needle` (all three, not just one).
- The FABRIC-doc-vs-otlp.rs instrument-name discrepancy is resolved (doc fixed, or code fixed, whichever is stale) and documented.
- Findings (pass/fail per step, any error text captured) are added back to this bead before closing.

Do not block closing this bead on step 5 ("Metrics path — apex Prometheus / Grafana") of the test plan, and do not treat prometheusremotewrite export failures as something that needs fixing.

title: needle stop --all help claims it stops workers; it only kills tmux sessions and orphans supervisors
description:
Companion to bf-4iwog (which covers `needle run --workspace`). This bead covers
the remaining help-text accuracy gaps, with `stop` as the serious one.

1. `needle stop --all` — CURRENTLY WRONG, and it matters

   Help says:   --all    Stop all needle workers

   Observed 2026-08-07 stopping a 17-worker fleet: `needle stop --all` killed the
   tmux sessions (the tmux server itself went away) but every supervisor survived,
   reparented to init:

     pid=1287492 state=S ppid=1 elapsed=05:31 children=2 --identifier alpha
     ... 8 identical

   They then ignored SIGINT entirely — both the supervisors and their children —
   while stuck in the pre-dispatch shell. Only SIGKILL cleared them. The command
   also printed its own contradiction:

     "kill attempt reported success but 3 process(es) still running"

   An operator reading the help concludes the fleet is stopped. It is not: the
   supervisors keep running, keep their claims, and can keep dispatching. This is
   the difference between "the fleet is down" and "the fleet looks down", and it
   is exactly the state you must NOT be in before rewriting git history or doing
   anything else that assumes quiescence.

   Suggested wording:

     --all
         Kill the tmux session of every registered worker.
         This does NOT reliably terminate the worker supervisors: a
         `needle run` process whose session is killed is commonly reparented
         to init and keeps running, and may ignore SIGINT. After this
         command, verify with `pgrep -af needle-stable run` and signal any
         survivors directly. See `needle cleanup` for session hygiene.

2. `needle supervise --workspace` — same ambiguity as bf-4iwog

   Help says:  Workspace to monitor (defaults to config workspace)
   Unclear whether the supervisor scales workers for that one workspace only, or
   uses it as a home while auto-discovery applies. Should state which.

3. `needle cleanup` is the model to copy — no change needed

   Its help already spells out exactly what the destructive flag does and when to
   use the safe form. The other subcommands should match that standard. Worth
   noting so nobody "fixes" it.

Acceptance: `needle stop --help` states that supervisors may survive and tells

title: 16.4a Author the beads_rust builtin descriptor (no claim, no batch)
description:
BrCliBeadStore is currently a chimera: beads_rust argv for create/dep/sync/list, but bead-forge argv for claim/release/split, bound to whichever binary discover() finds first.

bf-only code grafted into the beads_rust store:
- :1194-1220 claim_auto -> `bf claim --model/--harness/--harness-version --assignee --json`
- :1428-1437 claim -> `bf batch --json [{op:update,...}]`
- :1479-1486 release -> `bf batch`
- :1485/:1508 split_bead -> `bf batch`
- :1127-1136 a second, independent resolve_bf() serving only the above

beads_rust 0.1.28 has NEITHER `claim` NOR `batch` (verified: `br claim` -> "unrecognized subcommand", `br batch` -> "unrecognized subcommand"). It DOES have `update -s/--status --assignee` and a first-class `ready --json --limit`.

Deliverables:
- claim / release / clear_assignee use `update -s <status> --assignee ...` on the br binary. beads_rust never dropped --assignee, so no batch emulation is needed.
- claim_auto: no server-side claim exists. Implement as ready -> claim(id) and LOG the downgrade explicitly.
- split_bead: drop the override, inherit the non-atomic trait default (:646-668).
- Delete resolve_bf() at :1127 and run_bf_batch/run_bf_claim from this store.

Acceptance criteria:
- `grep -n "bf batch\|bf claim\|resolve_bf" src/bead_store/br_cli.rs` returns nothing.
- The TOCTOU window in the non-atomic claim_auto is documented in operator-facing docs, not only in a code comment — it changes multi-worker safety on beads_rust workspaces.
- Argv assertion tests pinned to real br 0.1.28.

See ADR-013 section 5.

title: bead-rs: revision is hardcoded to 1 on checkpoint export and never imported
description:
Found during the ADR-002 field-guide independent review (2026-08-12), recorded as I2.

read_all_issues - the reader used by BOTH flush paths (src/service/checkpoint.rs:3100 and :3181) - does not select the revision column and hardcodes revision: Some(1) at src/service/checkpoint.rs:4337. Neither import writer includes revision in its INSERT (src/service/checkpoint.rs:1863-1888 and :2928-2957), so the DB default of 1 applies on restore.

Verified empirically: a workspace whose live revisions were 4, 1, 2, 1 flushed four records all reading revision 1, and restoring into a fresh workspace produced 1, 1, 1, 1.

Live increments are correct (traced 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 across create/update/update/close). The loss is entirely in the checkpoint round-trip.

Impact: every optimistic-concurrency guard (--if-revision on update/release/close/reopen) is silently reset by a restore. A worker holding revision 4 will find the bead at revision 1 and its guard will behave incorrectly.

both Failed. Local full --lib suite on ex44: 1711 passed / 692.81s at a 2-core cap.

for 50 percent more CPU.

the time dependence eliminates it.

instead of real sleeps.

title: OTLP telemetry crashes worker on startup: tokio::spawn called before runtime is entered
description:
## Problem

Setting `telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled: true` in config crashes every worker
immediately at startup, before it claims a bead or does anything else.
Reproduced live on ex44 2026-08-08:

```
NEEDLE worker boot: creating tokio runtime...
NEEDLE worker boot: tokio runtime created
NEEDLE worker boot: initializing tracing subscriber...

thread 'main' (1864218) panicked at src/cli/mod.rs:826:5:
there is no reactor running, must be called from the context of a Tokio 1.x runtime
```

This is why OTLP has never actually worked fleet-wide despite the sink being
implemented and the collector/dashboard side being fully wired
(apexalgo-iad `needle-observability` collector, `dashboard.ardenone.com/needle`)
— nobody has been able to run a worker with it enabled without an instant crash.

## Root cause

`src/cli/mod.rs`:
- Line 936: `let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()...` constructs the
  runtime but does not enter it (no `rt.enter()` guard).
- Line 941: `init_tracing_subscriber(qualified_id.clone(), session_id.clone(), &config)?`
  runs synchronously, still outside any runtime context.
- Inside `init_tracing_subscriber` (same file, ~line 789), when
  `config.telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled` is true, line 831 calls
  `tokio::spawn(async move { ... })` to run the OTLP drop-monitor task.
  `tokio::spawn` requires an active runtime context (`Handle::current()`),
  which does not exist yet — the runtime isn't actually entered until
  `rt.block_on(...)` at line 964, well after `init_tracing_subscriber` has
  already returned (or in this case, panicked).

Classic Tokio gotcha: constructing a `Runtime` does not make it "current"
for the calling thread. You need either an `EnterGuard` from `rt.enter()`
held across the call, or the call needs to happen inside `rt.block_on(...)`.

## Fix

Hold an entered-runtime guard across the `init_tracing_subscriber` call in
`src/cli/mod.rs`, e.g.:

```rust
let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().context("failed to create tokio runtime")?;
let _rt_guard = rt.enter();   // <-- add this; keep alive at least through init_tracing_subscriber
eprintln!("NEEDLE worker boot: tokio runtime created");
...
init_tracing_subscriber(qualified_id.clone(), session_id.clone(), &config)?;
```

Alternative: move the OTLP layer construction (including the `tokio::spawn`
drop-monitor task) inside `rt.block_on(async { ... })` instead of calling it
from the synchronous portion of `main`. The `rt.enter()` guard is the
smaller, more localized change.

Check whether the same "runtime not entered" hazard applies to any other
`tokio::spawn` call reachable from synchronous startup code before the
first `rt.block_on` — `init_tracing_subscriber` may not be the only one.

## Acceptance criteria

- A worker launched with `telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled: true` boots
  successfully (no panic) and reaches its normal claim/dispatch loop.
- Add a regression test that constructs a `Runtime` without entering it,
  then calls `init_tracing_subscriber` with OTLP enabled, and asserts it
  does not panic (this must have caught the bug — write it to fail against
  the current code first, then pass after the fix).
- Live-verify on ex44: launch a real worker with OTLP enabled, confirm no
  crash, and confirm `dashboard.ardenone.com/needle` receives at least one
  event from it (this closes the loop on the whole OTLP-to-dashboard
  pipeline, not just the crash).

comments.text:
Live-verified 2026-08-12 on ex44 using a single scoped worker (identifier=otelverify, workspace=NEEDLE): flipped otlp_sink.enabled=true in the shared config.yaml just long enough to launch one worker (config is loaded once at process start, never hot-reloaded, so the rest of the live fleet was unaffected), then immediately reverted it.

Confirmed via binary provenance first: 192a2ab (the rt.enter() guard, bf-3s2b0) is an ancestor of source HEAD, and the installed ~/.local/bin/needle + needle-stable are both v0.2.19 built Aug 11 (after the fix), hash-matched.

Result: worker sailed straight through the former crash point (init_tracing_subscriber completed, no "no reactor running" panic) and reached "starting worker loop...". Ran healthy for ~4 minutes at low CPU before being intentionally stopped (SIGINT was ignored after ~8s, SIGKILL/tmux cleanup finished the job - matches the known SIGINT-ignored pattern from other NEEDLE incidents). No panic at any point, including at shutdown.

Crash bug itself looks fixed. Two things in this bead's acceptance criteria are still NOT verified, so leaving this open rather than closing:

1. Exactly one "sink flush failed: failed to flush logger provider" line appeared right as the worker loop started, and did not recur over the remaining ~4min. Isolated separately: an authenticated synthetic smoke test straight to the collector (needle-otel-ex44-apexalgo-iad-ts.ardenone.com:4318/v1/logs) got HTTP 200 {"partialSuccess":{}}, so the token/endpoint/auth path is confirmed good - this rules out a broken token or unreachable collector as the cause. The one flush failure is more likely a one-off startup-timing race (exporter batch task not fully ready for its first periodic flush) than a systemic break, but that is inference, not proof - nobody has read the actual reqwest/tonic error text behind "failed to flush logger provider" yet.

2. Never confirmed the worker's own real telemetry actually landed on dashboard.ardenone.com/needle (OAuth-gated, did not check) or in VictoriaLogs - the worker never claimed a bead in its ~4min run (NEEDLE workspace had nothing ready), so heartbeat may be the only event type it ever tried to emit.

Net: safe to consider the P0 crash resolved for planning purposes; bf-14jp7/bf-4p4dg still need the dashboard-visibility + full-duration-idle-with-heartbeats checks before this bead can honestly close.

title: Rebuild needle-ci-builder in CI and use it from the needle-ci template
description:
NEEDLE's own CI does not use NEEDLE's own builder image.

ci/Dockerfile.ci and ci/Dockerfile.ci-deps exist in this repo and produce
ronaldraygun/needle-ci-builder with tags latest and with-deps (dependencies
pre-compiled). But the needle-ci WorkflowTemplate starts from a bare
debian:bookworm and reinstalls apt packages, rustup and the gh apt repo on every
single run, then compiles 244 crates cold.

Worse, that image was last pushed 2026-04-25 -- over three months ago -- and
nothing in iad-ci rebuilds it, so its baked dependency layer no longer matches
Cargo.toml (opentelemetry 0.31, tonic 0.14 postdate it) and its rustup predates
the pinned-toolchain fix in rust-toolchain.toml.

Do:
- add a needle-ci-builder WorkflowTemplate + sensor in declarative-config under
  k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/, triggered by changes to Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock or
  ci/Dockerfile.ci*
- pin a semver tag, never latest and never a bare git SHA
- switch needle-ci's container image to it and delete the inline apt/rustup/gh
  install block

Blocked by the Cargo.lock bead: Dockerfile.ci-deps does COPY Cargo.toml Cargo.lock.

Acceptance: a needle-ci run performs no apt-get and no rustup install, and skips
compiling unchanged dependencies.

Three identical beads existed as of 2026-08-12 — bf-1o1sr (total beads 190), bf-61qvt (191), bf-8rep6 (192) — differing only in the bead count in the body. Left alone this accumulates one bead per occurrence forever, and each one is itself an open bead that inflates the count the next alert reports.

Fix: dedupe on firing. Either (a) find an existing open starvation bead for the same workspace and append a comment instead of creating, or (b) attach a stable dedup key (label 'alert:starvation:<workspace>') and skip creation when one is already open.

Context: these alerts were NOT spurious. 'Open beads exist but Pluck found none' was correct — the dependency graph had 10 beads stuck at status=blocked with no blockers, 21 inverted verify-blocks-build edges, and a 5-node cycle, so pluckable work was scarce while open beads existed. Graph repaired 2026-08-12; if the alert keeps firing after that, re-triage.

title: bead-rs: no conformance test asserts checkpoint round-trip fidelity
description:
Systemic gap behind three separate silent-data-loss defects found on 2026-08-12: revision reset to 1, issue_data destroyed, external_references destroyed. Each is individually filed; this bead covers the reason none of them was caught.

There is no test that populates every public field and side table, flushes a checkpoint, restores into a fresh empty workspace, and asserts the restored state equals the source state. Existing checkpoint tests cover format and mechanics, not fidelity.

Required: a conformance test that builds a maximally-populated workspace - every public issue field set to a non-default value, multiple labels, both dependency kinds, issue_data namespaces, external references, comments, events, a closed bead with closed_at and close_reason, a deferred bead, an assigned bead - flushes, restores into empty, and diffs the full state.

The assertion must be equality over the complete public surface, not a spot check of a few fields. Any field the round trip is not expected to preserve must be named explicitly in the test with a comment saying why, so that an intentional omission is visible and an accidental one fails.

This test would have caught all three defects. It should be written first and allowed to fail, so the fixes have a shared acceptance criterion.

Nothing asserts reference/comment/data survival across --merge, which is why bf-1cwrc passes CI. Extending the test to the merge path is an acceptance item on bf-1cwrc.

title: 16.16 Staged rollout — descriptor migration changes the claim path for the entire fleet
description:
bf-1awps deletes both BeadStore impls and replaces them with a descriptor-driven engine. That is the code path every worker uses to claim and close. A bad landing means the fleet cannot claim OR close — including the bead that broke it.

docs/notes/self-modification-risks.md, Incidents 1 and 2, is this exact scenario: a worker broke build.sh, `needle upgrade` rebuilt, hot-reload propagated to every running worker, entire fleet down simultaneously. The bead layer is a strictly worse blast radius than build.sh, because a broken claim path removes the mechanism by which the fix would be dispatched.

Deliverables:
- Version bump and a canary rollout through needle-testing before needle-stable (per ADR-005 hot-reload channel), NOT a direct install.
- A pre-flight gate: `needle bead-backend <name>` (bf-1hc0r) must pass for the resolved backend before a worker will boot on the new binary. Fail closed.
- A documented manual rollback: which binary to restore and how, written for someone whose fleet cannot currently claim beads. It must not assume a working NEEDLE.
- Land the engine behind config so the old path can be selected until the canary clears, if that is cheaper than a revert.

Acceptance criteria:
- The rollback procedure is executed once, deliberately, on a test worker — not merely written down.
- No step in the rollback depends on dispatching a bead.

See ADR-013 Consequences and docs/notes/self-modification-risks.md.

title: bead-rs: external references are silently dropped by the checkpoint round-trip
description:
Found during the ADR-002 field-guide independent review (2026-08-12). NOT previously recorded; discovered while auditing the full flush/restore path.

Reproduced with bead 0.1.1 in disposable workspaces:
  source: 2 issues, 3 labels, 1 blocks edge, 1 issue_data namespace, 1 external_reference, 2 events
  bead sync flush-only, then bead sync import-only --input CP --restore-into-empty --actor X
  restored: labels 3 OK, dependencies 1 OK, events 2 OK, issue_data 0 LOST, external_references 0 LOST, revision 3 -> 1 LOST

The checkpoint contains only issue and event record types. Labels and dependencies survive because they are carried inline as members of the issue record. There is no record type for external references and no member for them on the issue record, so every (namespace, key, value) written through bead ref add is destroyed by a flush/restore cycle.

WHY THIS IS THE MOST SEVERE OF THE ROUND-TRIP LOSSES: research/specs/native-field-guide-v1.md L168-170 and L213 make external references THE public mechanism binding rehydrated beads back to their source tracker IDs. The same document's rehearsal procedure flushes a checkpoint and restores it into a fresh workspace. As implemented, that rehearsal silently destroys the entire traceability chain it exists to prove.

Fix: carry external references in the checkpoint (either as an inline issue member alongside labels/dependencies, or as a distinct record_type) and write them on both import paths. Add round-trip coverage - see the conformance-test bead.

title: Split needle-ci into verify and release stages; gate release on a version change
description:
needle-ci is one monolithic pod that does setup, compile, test, a release
build and a GitHub publish, on every push to main -- guarded only by an
after-the-fact "does this tag already exist" check.

So roughly 95 percent of runs pay the full release cost, including
cargo build --release with lto=true and codegen-units=1 (the slowest possible
link configuration), only to discover the version did not change.

Do, in declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/needle-workflowtemplate.yml:
- stage 1 verify: fmt, clippy, cargo check as a fast fail, then the test suite
- stage 2 release: only runs when the version in Cargo.toml differs from the
  latest published tag
- keep the existing idempotent "release already exists, skip" guard as a backstop

Acceptance: a push that does not bump the version never runs cargo build
--release; a version bump still publishes exactly one release.
close_reason:
Split needle-ci into verify and release stages

The workflow now runs in two stages:
- Verify (always runs): fmt, clippy, cargo check, then test suite — no release build
- Release (conditional): only runs when Cargo.toml version differs from latest published GitHub release, does cargo build --release and GitHub publish

This avoids the expensive cargo build --release (with lto=true and codegen-units=1) on ~95% of pushes where the version hasn't changed, saving ~15+ minutes per run.

title: Decide + record ADR for concurrent same-repo worker isolation (plan §6.9 shared working directory)

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
GAP (plan-vs-artifacts): docs/plan/plan.md §6.9 (lines ~4085-4092) is the only flagged open question in the plan that is NOT resolved in code and NOT tracked by any existing bead or ADR.

EVIDENCE
- No per-worker isolation exists in src/: grep for `worktree` across src/ returns nothing. `bead.workspace` is passed through verbatim as the `{workspace}` template var into the dispatched agent process (src/dispatch/mod.rs), so every worker assigned to a repo runs its agent in the SAME working directory.
- The per-workspace claim flock (plan §6.1, ~line 219; src/claim/) guards only the CLAIMING step's `br update --claim`, NOT the EXECUTING phase. Once two workers are each dispatched into the same repo (with DISTINCT beads), their agents can run concurrent `git add`/`commit`/`reset --hard`/`checkout` in one shared tree for the full duration of both dispatches; one agent's `reset --hard`/`checkout` can discard another's uncommitted work.
- §6.6's flock protects only NEEDLE's own post-hoc Bead-Id trailer amend (src/commit_hook.rs), not the agents' concurrent work.
- Distinct from bf-1ne6u (atomic-claim duplicate-dispatch of the SAME bead) — §6.9 is the broader shared-working-directory hazard that persists even when claiming is correct and beads are distinct.
- docs/adr/ contains ADRs 001-010; none covers this. The plan explicitly states it 'should be captured as its own ADR before implementation ... a bigger design decision than the rest of Phase 6.'

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. New ADR under docs/adr/ (Context/Decision/Alternatives/Consequences) deciding between the two directions the plan names: (a) full git-worktree isolation per worker (incl. merge-back strategy + effect on commit_hook trailer injection), or (b) accept as a known constraint + add a needle-run help/docs callout that >1 worker per repo is unsafe unless beads avoid overlapping file/branch state.
2. plan.md §6.9 updated to reference the ADR and record the chosen direction (remove 'not yet decided').
3. If direction (a): follow-up implementation bead filed. If direction (b): the needle run --help / docs callout is added so the constraint is discoverable at point of use.

NOTE: plan Phase 7 (§7.1a cleanup pane_pid regression) and Phase 8 (§8.3 Explore rediscovery staleness) are BOTH already fixed in code (filter_sessions_for_cleanup_impl walks the process tree via find_needle_process_in_tree; ExploreStrand has rediscover_workspaces + rediscovery_cycles). Reviewer: Claude (Anthropic), author of neither the artifact nor any correction, not the schema implementation author, and not the author of the checkpoint fixes offered as evidence.

R12, R13 and R14 are CLOSED and independently reproduced. Implementation commit 0375fdc went past what the review required and fixed the merge defect instead of documenting it: merge now preserves structured data, external references and comments that an incoming record omits; content replacement advances the live revision token (existing>=incoming yields existing+1, else incoming is retained) so a pre-merge --if-revision holder cannot mutate replaced content; and both merge directions are covered by active conformance tests. Restore fidelity re-verified across revision, data (byte-identical incl. nested null), refs, comments, labels, dependencies, events and null description. cargo fmt --check clean, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo test exit 0 with 635 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored across 36 suites, no #[ignore] anywhere.

THREE REQUIRED REVISIONS REMAIN:

R15 (excluded from the accepted baseline) - section 4's claim 'Import validation rejects the invariant in both directions' is FALSE for sync import-only. Issue::validate() is reached only from stage_import (checkpoint.rs:2553) and stage_import_with_diagnostics (:2765); cmd_sync_import_only calls import_forensic_checkpoint, which stages through stage_forensic_checkpoint (:792) and checks no issue-level invariant. Verified twice: base_status=open carrying closed_at+close_reason, and base_status=closed carrying neither, both restored at exit 0 into a fresh workspace; doctor flags them afterwards, so detection works and rejection does not. --diagnostics is also never passed through on that command. Section 9 tells operators to rely on that enforcement point. Also excluded: section 9's clause 'import validation is bidirectional and diagnostic activation is all-or-nothing'.

R16 (additive text) - a second merge from the same origin store FAILS. validate_different_uuid_merge (:1689-1718) rejects any event-identity collision and a full checkpoint always re-emits from sequence 1; the same-UUID path (:1676-1684) is the mirror image. Minimal fleet loop reproduced: A creates+updates, flushes; B merges (1 inserted, rc=0); A updates, flushes; B merges again -> 'Internal error: Different-UUID merge has event identity conflict: (uuid, 1) already exists', rc=1, target left at the previous content. Every update/claim/close/release/reopen appends an event, so this is the second iteration of any realistic fleet loop. Fails loudly, no data loss.

R17 (additive text) - deletion of a projected collection cannot propagate through merge, the direct consequence of preserve-when-absent plus 'absent when empty'. Verified: source removed its only external reference and re-flushed; merging into a target holding a stale value left the stale value. Same for comments and data. Also, the whole cross-cutting merge rule set lives inside the external_references field entry while the comments and data entries never mention merge.

All round-two and round-three carve-outs are LIFTED. bf-4hr30, bf-xq4ds and bf-53b91 are fixed and verified on both restore and merge. bf-3siqo now matters only in the R15 sense: released 0.1.1 can mint invalid closed rows and no import path rejects them, so cutover must gate on doctor rather than on import.

Reviewer: Claude (Anthropic), author of neither the artifact nor any correction, not the schema implementation author, not the author of the checkpoint fixes.
Artifact: research/specs/native-field-guide-v1.md at bead-rs commit 805c7de

Scope: targeted to round-four R15-R17 and implementation commit 92701b7. No other section re-reviewed; all prior closures stand.

CLOSED:
- R15 forensic issue validation. validate_forensic_checkpoint (checkpoint.rs:1438-1442) now validates every staged issue before activation. Both directions rejected with nothing written, on --restore-into-empty AND --merge: 'Non-closed issues must not have closed_at or close_reason' and 'Closed issues must have a close_reason', rc=1, 0 issues. Section 9's replacement text is accurate and the round-four carve-out is lifted.
- R17 explicit empty projection deletion propagation. The exporter now emits data/external_references/comments unconditionally (:4518-4541, :4591); a new-producer record for an empty bead carries data={} refs=[] comments=[]. Source deleted all three, reflushed, merged: target went 1/1/1 -> 0/0/0.
- Legacy omission preservation. Stripping the three members from the same generation and merging left the target at 1/1/1 while scalar content advanced to notes='gen2'. 92701b7 also models this in the suite via remove_projected_collections.
- Repeated-merge hard failure is gone, and content-conflict handling is correct: tampering with an imported event's actor produced 'Event identity conflict: (uuid, 1) has different content', rc=1, target title and event count unchanged.

fmt clean, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo test exit 0 with 635 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored across 36 suites, no #[ignore] anywhere. Working tree clean, HEAD = origin/main = 805c7de, divergence 0 0.

R18 REMAINS (the only open item, excluded from the accepted baseline):
Section 4 claims repeated merges 'accept an identical event-history prefix and import only its new suffix'. The suffix-only half is FALSE. import_events uses INSERT OR IGNORE (:1938-1955) and supplies no sequence, but the events table's only uniqueness is 'sequence INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT' (migrations.rs:121-129); (origin_store_uuid, origin_event_sequence) carries a NON-UNIQUE index (migrations.rs:236). Nothing can ever be ignored, and validate_event_prefix only decides whether the merge may proceed.

Measured, one source merged three times into one target as it gained one event per round:
  after merge 1: 1 origin event  (seq 1 x1)
  after merge 2: 3 origin events (seq 1 x2, seq 2 x1)
  after merge 3: 6 origin events (seq 1 x3, seq 2 x2, seq 3 x1)   source has 3
  rows with an origin identity = 6, distinct identities = 3
Growth is quadratic in merge count and is consumer-visible: 'bead changes --since 0 --json' on that target reports total_available: 9, each duplicate its own mutation. It also falsifies section 6's 'ordered by (origin_store_uuid, origin_event_sequence)' identity and 'monotonically contiguous integer within the origin store' in a merge target. The conformance suite misses it because the repeated-merge test asserts only that the three collections reach zero; it never counts events.

FIX, either:
1. CREATE UNIQUE INDEX events_origin_identity_unique ON events (origin_store_uuid, origin_event_sequence) WHERE origin_store_uuid IS NOT NULL  -- partial is required because local events carry NULL origin columns. NOTE the index CANNOT be created on already-duplicated data (fails with UNIQUE constraint failed on the probe target), so the migration needs a dedupe step for any workspace that has merged twice. Or skip in import_events the identities validate_event_prefix already matched.
2. Or correct the claim - but then section 6's identity/contiguity statements need the same treatment plus a known_implementation_deviations entry. Option 1 keeps more accepted text true.
Add an event-count assertion to the repeated-merge conformance coverage either way.

ALL prior carve-outs are LIFTED, including both round-four exclusions (the section 4 closed_at sentence and the section 9 bidirectional-validation clause). R18 is one clause plus a five-line migration or a skip, plus one assertion. Next revision gets a new hash and an unconditional-acceptance review scoped to that single item.

title: OTLP sink config schema diverges from plan.md (tls/signals/timeout_ms unimplemented)
description:
Found 2026-08-06 during the stash audit. Three April stashes on the merged
feat/hoop-dispatch-tag branch defined OtlpTlsConfig, OtlpSignalsConfig,
OtlpProtocol and OtlpCompression as real types. What landed in main instead is a
flattened OtlpSinkConfig, and it no longer matches the schema plan.md documents.

plan.md documents this OTLP block (twice: sections at lines 1908-1925 and
2495-2510):

  telemetry:
    otlp:
      timeout_ms: 5000
      tls:
        insecure: false
        ca_file: ""
      signals:
        traces: true
        metrics: true
        logs: true

src/config/mod.rs OtlpSinkConfig actually has:
  - tls: String            <- plan documents a NESTED MAP (insecure, ca_file)
  - timeout_secs: u64      <- plan documents timeout_ms
  - (no signals field)     <- per-signal traces/metrics/logs toggles absent

Consequences:
  1. tls is the serious one. A config written per the plan supplies a YAML map
     where serde expects a String, which is a deserialization error, not a
     silent fallback.
  2. timeout_ms and signals are silently ignored. src/config/mod.rs sets
     deny_unknown_fields nowhere (grep count: 0), so unknown keys are dropped
     and the user gets the 10s default while believing they set 5s.
  3. There is no way to export traces but suppress metrics/logs, which the plan
     explicitly offers.

Not verified end-to-end: attempting to load a plan-conformant workspace
.needle.yaml produced no otlp keys AND no error, because the workspace override
path ignored the file entirely. That is a separate known issue and it also means
this misconfiguration would fail quietly rather than loudly.

Decide and then make plan and code agree:
  - either implement the documented schema (nested tls, signals, timeout_ms,
    with serde aliases so timeout_secs keeps working), or
  - amend plan.md to document the flattened schema that actually shipped.

Adding deny_unknown_fields to the telemetry config structs is worth doing either
way, so a typo in an OTLP key is a loud failure instead of a silent default.

Acceptance: a config file copied verbatim out of plan.md loads without error and
produces the values it specifies; or plan.md matches the implemented schema.

title: Canary expectations are stale (expect status 'done'), so every upgrade is rejected 0/4 on ex44
description:
Found 2026-08-02 upgrading ex44 to v0.2.16.

'needle upgrade' downloaded 0.2.16, ran canary validation, scored 0/4 and
rejected the binary. The rejection is NOT a regression in the new build — the
canary expectations under ~/.needle/canary/expected/ are dated 2026-03-21 and
have not tracked bead-forge's vocabulary since.

expected/canary-bzl.yaml (the happy-path test) asserts:

    final_status: done

bead-forge has no 'done' status. Statuses actually in use across real
workspaces are: open, in_progress, blocked, closed, completed, pending, ready.
A closed bead reports 'closed'. NEEDLE knows this — src/types/mod.rs carries the
comment "br show --json emits 'closed' for done beads. Treat as equivalent".
So canary-bzl is unsatisfiable by ANY needle binary, old or new, and the canary
gate can never pass.

The observed run looked behaviourally fine: canary-bzl closed, canary-nnw
closed, canary-8ej blocked, canary-atw in_progress. All four were still scored
as failures, so the other three expectations are likely stale in the same way
(canary-8ej wants final_status 'open' plus a 'failure-count:1' label;
canary-nnw wants 'open' for a timeout).

Impact: the upgrade path on any host with a canary workspace is permanently
blocked, and the failure presents as 'the new binary is bad' rather than 'the
test fixtures rotted'. bench has no canary workspace, so it promoted 0.2.16
straight to :stable and its workers hot-reloaded correctly — good evidence the
binary itself is fine.

Not urgent for correctness on ex44: it still has the deprecated br shim at
~/.local/bin/br, so its 0.2.14 workers' 'br close' continues to work. The cost
is that ex44 stays on old binaries.

Fix direction: refresh the four expected/*.yaml against current bead-forge
vocabulary, and add an assertion that each expected final_status is a status
bf can actually produce, so this rots loudly next time. Also surface per-test
detail — 'needle canary --status' only prints channel state, giving no clue
which expectation failed or why.

Acceptance: 'needle upgrade' on ex44 passes canary and promotes to :stable.

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
Fuller diagnosis 2026-08-02 — NOT a fixture-only fix. Five independent defects; the gate has almost certainly never worked.

1. NO BEAD RESET. CanaryRunner::run() has no reset/seed step — grep for reset_bead/seed/set_status in src/canary/mod.rs returns nothing. The four beads keep whatever terminal state the last run left (now: canary-bzl=closed, canary-nnw=closed, canary-8ej=blocked, canary-atw=in_progress). A worker cannot claim a closed bead, so later runs do nothing.

2. RACE. run_test() spawns `needle run --workspace ... --count 1` WITHOUT NEEDLE_INNER=1. That form detaches into tmux and returns immediately — the upgrade output prints "Started worker ... in tmux session / Attach with: tmux attach -t ...". So child.try_wait() returns exit 0 within milliseconds and get_actual_outcome() reads the bead long before any agent work. The exit code compared for Success/Failure is the launcher's, not the agent's.

3. StateMachine UNIMPLEMENTED. get_actual_outcome() hardcodes state_transitions: Vec::new() ("Not tracked in basic canary tests"). outcomes_match() does transitions.iter().all(|t| actual.state_transitions.contains(t)); against an always-empty vec any non-empty expected list is unsatisfiable. canary-atw could only pass with zero transitions, i.e. vacuously.

4. STALE VOCABULARY. ExpectedOutcome::default_final_status() returns "done", and expected/canary-bzl.yaml asserts final_status: done. bead-forge has no 'done' status (open/in_progress/blocked/closed/completed/pending/ready). The rot is in the source default too, so omitting the field does not help.

5. USES br. get_actual_outcome() runs Command::new(&self.br_path).args(["show", id, "--json"]). On a host without the deprecated br shim the canary errors instead of validating — same root cause as bf-15tys.

Consequence: the canary cannot pass for ANY binary, which is why 'needle upgrade' on ex44 rejected v0.2.16 at 0/4. Nothing is wrong with that build — bench has no canary workspace, promoted it, and both workers hot-reloaded and now emit 'bf close'.

Real fix spans all five points plus refreshed fixtures plus a CI cycle — materially more than editing YAML. Until then the gate protects nothing; it is a permanent block that presents as "the new binary is bad".

title: cargo clippy --all-targets fails on examples/validate_p95_values.rs (blocks the clippy gate)
description:
Discovered 2026-08-06 while reviewing stashes.

cargo clippy --all-targets currently FAILS (not warns) on:

  error: this comparison involving the minimum or maximum element for this
  type contains a case that is always true or always false
    --> examples/validate_p95_values.rs:37:27
     |
  37 |         let is_positive = p95 >= 0;
     = help: because 0 is the minimum value for this type, this comparison is
       always true
     = note: #[deny(clippy::absurd_extreme_comparisons)] on by default

p95 is an unsigned type, so p95 >= 0 is a tautology and the guard does nothing.

This blocks bf-528j7: a clippy gate cannot be added to needle-ci until
--all-targets compiles. cargo clippy --tests is clean (exit 0, zero warnings)
as of 2fb89ed, so only the examples target is affected.

the intent was to validate the value is non-zero / within range.

Acceptance: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings exits 0.
close_reason: Fixed clippy error by removing tautological p95 >= 0 comparison. Since u128 is unsigned and always non-negative, the check was meaningless. title: Worker boot panics when telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled=true: tokio::spawn called outside runtime context
close_reason: Duplicate of bf-4icyq — see comment.

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
Reproduced 2026-08-08 on lab (100.81.129.38), 100% reproducible across both v0.2.16 and v0.2.19 binaries, so it's not a version regression — it's config-gated.

Root cause: src/cli/mod.rs (~line 826 in v0.2.19, ~741 in v0.2.16), inside the worker-boot tracing-subscriber init. When telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled=true, the OTLP branch calls tokio::spawn(async move { ... drop_rx.recv() ... }) to build the drop-event logging task — but this init function runs synchronously, before the worker's tokio runtime is entered. Panic: 'there is no reactor running, must be called from the context of a Tokio 1.x runtime'. Every single worker-boot attempt crashed immediately after 'initializing tracing subscriber' in stderr, before ever reaching bead_store_discover.

needle rollback (0.2.19->0.2.16) hits the same class of bug on its own shutdown path (src/telemetry/otlp.rs:463), confirming this pattern isn't new.

Repro condition: config's telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled=true (lab's was pointed at http://needle-otel-lab-apexalgo-iad-ts.ardenone.com:4318). Workaround applied on lab: set otlp_sink.enabled=false in ~/.config/needle/config.yaml (original backed up to config.yaml.bak-otlp-panic-2026-08-08). Fix needed: move the tokio::spawn call to run after runtime entry (e.g. spawn from within the async worker-boot future, or use runtime.handle().spawn() with an explicitly-passed Handle, or build the drop-channel task via a plain OS thread instead of tokio::spawn).

title: classify_error_code has 153 duplicated error codes; 46 match arms unreachable
description:
Found 2026-08-02 while unblocking the v0.2.16 release.

src/types/mod.rs classify_error_code() enumerates 710 distinct Rust error
codes across category arms, but 153 of them appear more than once. Because
match arms are evaluated in order, the second and later occurrences are dead:
rustc reports 46 'unreachable pattern' errors under
cargo clippy --lib -- -D warnings.

The practical effect is silent misclassification. E0748-E0757, for example,
are claimed by the Syntax arm and then listed again under 'Macro expansion
errors' — so they classify as Syntax, not Macro. Same for the E0750/E0758-E0761
overlap between ScopeVisibility and Macro, and E0781-E0783 between TraitImpl,
BorrowChecker and Macro.

This is not cosmetic: the whole point of the feature (bf-5pcn6/bf-59d0e/bf-5s7br)
is routing on error category, and 46 codes route to the wrong one.

The enumeration also covers codes rustc does not emit (E0800-E0999 are listed
wholesale as Syntax), which inflates the arms and makes the overlap hard to
see by eye.

Reproduce: cargo clippy --lib -- -D warnings

Fix direction: derive the mapping from a single ordered table keyed by code so
duplicates are impossible by construction, or at minimum de-duplicate and add a
unit test asserting no code appears in more than one category. Trim codes rustc
never emits.

Note this merged unverified because needle-ci has been wedged since
2026-07-31 (declarative-config bf-2ls).

title: Fix needle-ci retryStrategy: it masks every failure as 'Max duration limit exceeded'
description:
Both failed runs on 2026-08-06 reported "Max duration limit exceeded" at the
workflow level. That is wrong and it cost real diagnosis time -- the actual
failure was exit code 101 from a single failing test.

Cause: retryStrategy.backoff.maxDuration is 10m, but one attempt takes 22-26 min.
maxDuration is the total retry budget measured from the first attempt, so retries
can never fire, and the retry machinery relabels an ordinary test failure with a
misleading message.

Secondary: retryPolicy is OnError, which would not retry a test failure anyway.
The transient-network case the template's comment justifies wants
OnTransientError.

Do, in declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/needle-workflowtemplate.yml:
remove backoff.maxDuration (or raise it well above one attempt) and switch
retryPolicy to OnTransientError.

Acceptance: a failing test surfaces as a test failure with the failing test name,
not as a duration message.

title: needle-ci pod cannot schedule: 2000m/4Gi request + large-node selector loses to concurrent kaniko builds
description:
Observed live 2026-08-06 on needle-ci-8x2jj. The pod sat Pending for 78 minutes
and never started -- zero compilation, zero tests -- and is on track to be killed
by activeDeadlineSeconds (7200) at 13:18:25Z having done nothing at all.

Scheduler verdict (47 retries over 78 min):

  0/6 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient cpu, 3 Insufficient memory,
  3 node(s) did not match Pod node affinity/selector.

Why:
  - The pod carries nodeSelector servers.ngpc.rxt.io/class=ch.vs1.large-iad,
    which excludes the three compute1-4 nodes (1500m / 2.6Gi) outright. Only the
    three compute1-8 nodes (3500m / 6.16Gi) are ever eligible.
  - Those three are not empty. They also host forgejo, eventbus-default-js,
    calico, armor and victorialogs. Free CPU at the time of writing was 900m,
    900m and 1100m; free memory 1820Mi, 988Mi and 1948Mi.
  - needle-ci requests 2000m CPU and 4Gi. It fits on none of them.
  - The dominant occupier was a single ACB build: acb-bots-build-5kv8k ran FIVE
    concurrent kaniko pods at 1000m/2048Mi each (5 CPU, 10Gi total), spread
    1/2/2 across exactly those three nodes, for 99+ minutes.

So one unrelated multi-container build can monopolise every node needle-ci is
allowed to run on, and needle-ci then burns its entire 2h deadline in Pending.
This is a scheduling failure, not a slow build, and it is invisible in the
"Failed" status -- the workflow reports a deadline breach with no logs.

The template comment says the 2000m/4Gi request was deliberately sized against
the biggest node. That reasoning accounted for node capacity but not for the
resident system pods or for concurrent workflows.

Options, in declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/needle-workflowtemplate.yml:
  - lower the CPU request so the pod fits alongside normal residents (the limit
    can stay high -- requests gate scheduling, limits gate throttling)
  - drop the large-node selector once the request fits a compute1-4 node
  - cap ACB kaniko parallelism, or give CI workflows a PriorityClass so a
    release gate is not starved by an image build
  - shorten the effective runtime so the deadline is not spent queuing (see
    bf-4icmm, bf-4jdlu, bf-53ihi)

Acceptance: needle-ci reaches Running within a few minutes of submission even
while another multi-pod build is in flight.

title: 16.5b identity_pattern verification — reject the br shim masquerading as beads_rust
description:
~/.local/bin/br is a shell shim that logs the caller and execs ~/.local/bin/bf. The real beads_rust binary is ~/.cargo/bin/br v0.1.28. So `which br` returns something that speaks the bf dialect — this is exactly how ADR-013 section 5 went unnoticed for as long as it did.

A resolver that finds `br` on PATH and assumes beads_rust will bind the beads_rust adapter to bead-forge all over again, in a new place.

Deliverables:
- After resolving a candidate binary, VERIFY the backend identity rather than trusting the filename. `br --version` on the shim prints `bf <version>` (it execs bf), so a version-string check is sufficient and cheap — but confirm that empirically before relying on it.
- On mismatch (filename says br, identity says bf), fail loudly with an actionable message naming both paths. Do not silently fall back.
- Same check for a bf-named binary that is actually something else.

Acceptance criteria:
- A test with a fixture shim (a script execing a different fake binary) proves the mismatch is detected and reported, not silently accepted.
- The error message names the resolved path AND the identity actually found.

See ADR-013 section 5 and Evidence.

title: OTLP export silently dies after first transient flush failure, never recovers
description:
## Problem

Confirmed live on ex44 2026-08-12: real fleet workers (rota-1, hoop-1) converted to telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled=true both boot clean (bf-3s2b0/192a2ab's crash fix holds) and hit exactly ONE "NEEDLE telemetry: sink flush failed: failed to flush logger provider" line right as the worker loop starts. That single line is the LAST OTLP-related log line either process ever produces.

Over the following ~5 minutes, both workers stayed completely healthy doing real work (heartbeat files updating every ~30s, rota-1 on bf-576h8, hoop-1 moved from bf-1sy9t to bf-qt5hn - i.e. actually completing/cycling beads), proving the worker/local file_sink telemetry path is unaffected. But queried needle-dashboard's /api/dashboard directly (via a scoped port-forward, bypassing the OAuth gate) 8 times over 160s: zero events, zero worker entries for rota-1 or hoop-1 ever appeared. active_workers stayed 0 the whole time.

By contrast, a separate synthetic curl POST straight to the collector's /v1/logs endpoint (with valid authentication) DID land and IS visible on the dashboard (worker_id=unknown, event_type=test.smoke, timestamped 06:14:04Z) - so the collector, VictoriaLogs, and dashboard side of the pipe are all confirmed working. The break is specifically in NEEDLE's own OTLP exporter: after the first flush failure, it appears to stop trying entirely rather than retrying on the next periodic flush (metrics_interval_secs=10 in this config - there should have been ~30 more flush attempts in that window if the exporter were still alive).

## Hypothesis (not confirmed - nobody has read the actual underlying error)

The "sink flush failed: failed to flush logger provider" message wraps whatever the real reqwest/tonic/opentelemetry-sdk error was, but that inner error is not logged - only the wrapper text is. Two candidate mechanisms:
1. The periodic export task (likely spawned via the same tokio::spawn pattern bf-3s2b0 just fixed for the drop-monitor task) panics or returns early on its first failure and is never restarted - a sibling bug to the one bf-3s2b0 fixed, same file/area (src/telemetry/otlp.rs), different task.
2. The BatchLogProcessor's background worker thread/task exits after an unhandled error from its export attempt, which is normal-ish behavior for some OTel SDK batch processors on certain error classes, but would mean NEEDLE needs its own retry/restart wrapper around it - the SDK default is not to silently resume.

## What to check

- Read the actual error via a debug build or by adding a Display of the underlying error to the "sink flush failed" log line (currently just "failed to flush logger provider" with no source/cause chain rendered).
- Check whether the OTLP log-export background task/thread is still alive after the first failure (thread list, tokio task count, or an explicit liveness marker).
- Check whether this is a race specific to worker startup (first flush landing before something else - e.g. the collector's receiver - is fully warmed up) vs a persistent per-connection failure (e.g. HTTP/2 connection pool issue, DNS caching a bad result once).
- Reproduce with RUST_LOG=debug or equivalent to get more detail than the current single-line warning.

## Acceptance criteria

- Root cause of the first flush failure identified (actual error text captured, not just the wrapper message).
- Fix confirmed: a worker with otlp_sink.enabled=true runs for 5+ minutes, its heartbeat/claim/dispatch events are visible on needle-dashboard's /api/dashboard without needing a synthetic/manual event to prove the pipe works.
- If the fix is "retry on transient export failure", add a regression test forcing one export failure and asserting the exporter keeps trying on subsequent flushes rather than going permanently silent.

## Context

Found while live-verifying bf-3s2b0/192a2ab (the OTLP startup-crash fix) against real fleet workers per user request. That fix is solid - crash is gone - but this is a second, distinct bug in the same area that was masked by the crash bug (nobody could get a worker to stay alive long enough with OTLP on to notice this one until now).
close_reason:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED AND FIXED. build_http_providers() in src/telemetry/otlp.rs called .with_endpoint(config.endpoint.clone()) for all three OTLP HTTP exporters (traces/metrics/logs), passing the bare configured endpoint with no per-signal path. opentelemetry-otlp only auto-appends /v1/traces, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs when resolving from an OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*_ENDPOINT env var - NOT when .with_endpoint() is called programmatically, which is what NEEDLE does. Every HTTP export request has therefore always hit the collector's bare root (e.g. http://needle-otel-ex44-.../4318/) and gotten a 404, silently and permanently, for every worker that has ever run with otlp_sink.enabled=true.

Confirmed by first fixing the swallowed-error bug (the "sink flush failed: failed to flush logger provider" log line only showed Display, not the wrapped cause - fixed to show the full anyhow chain), then reproducing: the real error was reqwest::Error { kind: Status(404, None), url: ".../4318/" }. Cross-checked directly against the opentelemetry-otlp 0.31.1 crate source (vendored locally) - confirmed with_endpoint() is used verbatim with no path appended, matching the crate's own test suite behavior.

Fix (commit 40de7e3): append the correct /v1/{signal} suffix per exporter before calling with_endpoint(), trimming a trailing slash on the base endpoint first. build_grpc_providers is unaffected (gRPC has no per-signal URL paths).

Live-verified with a scoped diagnostic worker (identifier=otel-fixcheck, local debug build, workspace NEEDLE): boots clean, claims a real bead (bf-47ab9), and its full event stream (worker.booting, bead.claim.attempted/succeeded, build.heartbeat, agent.routing_decision, agent.dispatched, transform.started, worker.state_transition, rate_limit.allowed, init.step.*) is now visible on dashboard.ardenone.com/needle via direct API query - the first real (non-synthetic) worker telemetry this pipeline has ever successfully delivered end-to-end.

Also fixed in the same investigation: a fresh, unrelated compile break on main (bf-5stm4, TimeoutReason missing Display) that was blocking any local build.

title: needle-ci red: exit 101 (rust panic) + max duration exceeded on two runs; four runs queued concurrently
description:
Two `needle-ci` runs failed on iad-ci with the same signature, 9h and 11h
before 2026-08-06 12:35Z:

- `needle-ci-vnmhd` — workflow message "Max duration limit exceeded",
  node exit **101**
- `needle-ci-x2wx2` — identical

Exit 101 is the Rust convention for a panic / `cargo test` failure, so this
is a real red suite, not just the duration cap. The duration message means
the run also hit the workflow's max-duration before finishing.

Relates to the epic bf-21tze ("cut NEEDLE CI from a ~50min red run to a
<10min green run") — this bead records the concrete current failure so the
epic has a reproducible starting point rather than a general description.

## Also observed: needle-ci pile-up

At 12:35Z there were **four** needle-ci workflows queued simultaneously
(`needle-ci-8x2jj` 76m, `-f46kr` 69m, `-kz4qz` 62m, `-xt8tz` 62m), none of
them able to schedule a pod. Each push spawns another run while the previous
ones are still queued, so the queue grows faster than it drains. Consider a
concurrency limit / `synchronization` semaphore on the needle-ci template so
only one run is in flight per branch.

## Reproducing

Pod logs are gone (`podGC: OnPodCompletion`). Resubmit with a
`podGC: OnWorkflowCompletion` override, or stream logs while running.

title: Worker::check_hot_reload is dead code - hot-reload has never actually run
description:
src/worker/mod.rs:3059, #[allow(dead_code)] async fn check_hot_reload(&mut self) - doc comment says 'Called between LOGGING and SELECTING', but there is no call site anywhere (grepped the whole src tree). Introduced in c32da81 (2026-03-21, hot-reload protocol and rollback) and has apparently never been wired into the actual state machine since. The only other spawn/binary-related mechanism, src/spawn_path/mod.rs's check_spawn_path_at_boot, is purely a detect-and-log guardrail (emits spawn_path.modified_in_place telemetry, no re-exec) called once at worker boot - it cannot substitute for live hot-reload either.

Practical effect: replacing needle-stable (or the spawn-path binary) has ZERO effect on any currently-running worker - they keep running their original in-memory image indefinitely regardless of what needle upgrade / manual promote() does to disk. This likely explains why past fleet deploys in memory/incident history describe manually killing+relaunching worker PIDs rather than observing an actual live hot-reload - that was probably always the real mechanism, not the documented one.

Discovered 2026-08-12 while redeploying the bf-6a617 fix and checking whether it was safe to update needle-stable with 10 real workers running. Not fixed here - wiring in a real call site (e.g. in the LOGGING->SELECTING transition, matching the doc comment's own claim) is a separate, non-trivial task: needs to actually test the re-exec path works (self-exec with --resume, preserving worker identity/heartbeat), not just remove the dead_code attribute.

Umbrella tracking bead for ADR-013 / plan.md Phase 16. Closes when every child below closes.

Goal: let a NEEDLE worker drive a bead-rs (`bead`) workspace as well as bead-forge (`bf`) and the deprecated `br` shim, selected by configuration rather than a hardcoded PATH probe. Driven by the game-of-life project in the agent-sandbox cluster, whose workspace is bead-rs-backed and which stock NEEDLE cannot claim from at all.

The BeadStore trait (src/bead_store/mod.rs:546) is already the right seam and does not change shape. What changes is everything leaking past it: five hardcoded copies of the bf/br resolution chain, a bf-specific dialect baked into method bodies, prompt text handing agents literal `bf` commands, and a bead-forge-specific version handshake.

Reference: docs/adr/013-pluggable-bead-cli-backends.md, docs/plan/plan.md Phase 16.

description:
New src/bead_store/bead_cli.rs implementing the existing BeadStore trait against bead-rs (`bead`). Surface enumerated from ~/bead-rs/src/cli.rs at commit fa30574.

Dialect specifics (each differs from bf in a way that fails loudly at runtime and silently in review):
- claim/release/clear_assignee: plain `update --status ... --assignee ...` / `update --status open --clear-assignee`. bead-rs UpdateOptions (cli.rs:444) KEPT the --assignee that bf 0.4.1 removed, so these are SIMPLER here than on bf — no batch emulation needed.
- claim_auto: `claim --assignee A --json`. Omit --model/--harness/--harness-version — bead-rs ClaimOptions (cli.rs:370) does not accept them. Selection falls back to bead-rs own --policy (default fifo-v1).
- create_bead: `--description` (not --body), repeated `--label`, no --json. bead-rs create prints the bare issue ID on stdout.
- add_dependency: `--kind blocks` (not --type). Confirm positional order against the installed binary before landing.
- full_rebuild: bead-rs `sync --import-only` REQUIRES --input plus exactly one of --restore-into-empty / --merge (SyncCommand, cli.rs:667). The current bare call would fail.
- list/show/update --status/reopen/close --reason/label add|remove/doctor [--repair]/sync --flush-only all match and need no special handling.
- split_bead: deliberately NOT overridden. bead-rs has no `batch` subcommand, so it inherits the non-atomic trait default (:646-668) and its documented orphaned-child crash window. Log at split time that the atomic path is unavailable on this backend.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every trait method implemented; no todo!()/unimplemented!().
- Known limitations (no atomic split, no velocity-scoring metadata) are logged at runtime, not silently swallowed.
- fmt + clippy + full suite green on iad-ci.

title: is_pid_alive treats zombie workers as alive, fooling supervisor capacity accounting (GH #12, compounding)
description:
Compounding half of GH #12 (https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/issues/12), same report as bf-12bim (reap sweep). Full rationale: ADR-010 (docs/adr/010-supervisor-zombie-reaping.md), plan.md Phase 14.2.

Confirmed against source: registry::is_pid_alive (src/registry/mod.rs:28-52) checks liveness via kill(pid, 0) == 0 (with errno ESRCH/EPERM disambiguation). kill(pid, 0) succeeds for a zombie (state Z) exactly as it does for a genuinely running process — a zombie still holds a PID table entry, it just hasn't been reaped yet (see bf-12bim). This is not a hypothetical concern: Supervisor::tick() (src/supervisor/mod.rs:308-336) filters registered workers with is_pid_alive(w.pid) (line 316) to compute alive_count, then gates new spawns on alive_count >= self.config.max_workers (line 335). So every unreaped worker zombie is counted as alive by the supervisor's own tick, artificially inflating alive_count and potentially blocking new worker spawns at exactly the moment real capacity exists. The reporter's issue explicitly connects this to a 'false max_workers capacity and silent hung supervise logs' observation during their cutover soak (compounded on their host by an unrelated large zombie population from PID 1 not reaping its own children).

strand::mend's liveness check (src/strand/mend.rs:707) also calls registry::is_pid_alive and inherits this same bug.

Suggested fix (decision in ADR-010): on Linux, additionally check /proc/<pid>/stat's process-state field (the character after the second ')' in the comm field, robust to command names containing parentheses) and treat state Z as NOT alive, even though kill(pid, 0) still succeeds for it. Fall back to today's kill(pid, 0)-only behavior on non-Linux platforms (no /proc on macOS) and whenever /proc/<pid>/stat is unreadable for any reason (permissions, race with process exit) — never MORE strict than today's check, only additionally strict for the one case (Z) that today's check gets provably wrong.

Explicitly out of scope (per ADR-010): src/cli/mod.rs has its own separate, simpler duplicate is_pid_alive (kill(pid,0)==0, no errno handling) used for needle status/needle cleanup display/filtering, not supervisor capacity gating. It has the same zombie blind spot in principle but fixing it is not necessary to resolve GH #12's reported impact — leave it as a smaller, separate follow-up if status/cleanup output for zombies becomes its own complaint.

Acceptance criteria:
- registry::is_pid_alive returns false for a deliberately-created, deliberately-unreaped zombie PID on Linux.
- Behavior unchanged for non-Linux platforms and for genuinely-alive/genuinely-dead PIDs on all platforms (existing liveness tests still pass).
- Regression test reproducing the reporter's capacity-hang scenario: a zombie worker in the registry no longer counts toward alive_count in Supervisor::tick().
- cargo test --lib passes; no clippy warnings; needle-ci green on push.
close_reason: Fixed by 81b0995 (bf-z3yp0): registry::is_pid_alive now checks /proc/<pid>/stat state on Linux and treats Z (zombie) as not-alive, so Supervisor::tick()'s alive_count/max_workers capacity gate can no longer be fooled by unreaped zombies. GH #12.

title: bead-rs: dep add with an invalid --kind reports success and writes nothing
description:
Found during the ADR-002 field-guide independent review (2026-08-12), recorded as I4.

add_dependency does not validate kind, and the insert uses INSERT OR IGNORE (src/service/dependencies.rs:128-137), which swallows the DB CHECK (kind IN ('blocks','relates_to')) violation at src/store/migrations.rs:162.

Verified empirically:
  $ bead dep add t-fc96fb48 t-1294272c --kind parent-child
  Added dependency: t-fc96fb48 related to t-1294272c
  exit=0
  $ sqlite3 .beads/beads.db 'SELECT * FROM dependencies'
  t-fc96fb48|t-aa8b9d29|blocks     # the bogus edge was silently dropped

Kind validation exists only on the dry-run path (src/service/dryrun.rs:331-334), so --dry-run rejects what the real command accepts.

Fix: validate kind before insert and return exit 4 on an unknown kind; reserve INSERT OR IGNORE for the genuine idempotency case.

title: Add trace sanitization performance benchmark (Phase 4 success criterion)
description:
Phase 4 success criteria include: 'Keyword pre-filter (Aho-Corasick) skips irrelevant rules; sanitization adds <10ms per trace file.'

title: bead-rs: bead data content does not survive a checkpoint round-trip
description:
Found during the ADR-002 field-guide independent review (2026-08-12), recorded as I3.

Structured data lives only in the issue_data table (src/store/migrations.rs:182-189), reachable via bead data set|get|list|remove. Every issue loader hardcodes data: None (src/service/issues.rs:278 and :322, src/service/lifecycle.rs:502, src/service/query.rs:400, src/service/checkpoint.rs:4338).

Verified empirically: after bead data set, a flush emits the issue with no data member, and a restore into a fresh workspace yields SELECT COUNT(*) FROM issue_data = 0.

Impact: bead data content is not durable across checkpoint/restore. Combined with the rule that agents must never hand-write checkpoint JSONL, any data namespace written through the public CLI is unrecoverable after a restore.

title: Implement ADR-010: supervisor tick() WNOHANG reap sweep + zombie-aware is_pid_alive
description: Implements the fix decided in docs/adr/010-supervisor-zombie-reaping.md for GH #12 / bf-12bim: (1) add a waitpid(-1, WNOHANG) reap loop at the top of Supervisor::tick() in src/supervisor/mod.rs, looping until it returns 0 or -1/ECHILD; (2) harden registry::is_pid_alive to additionally check /proc/<pid>/stat's state field on Linux and treat state Z (zombie) as not-alive, falling back to today's kill(pid,0)-only behavior elsewhere; explicitly leave cli::is_pid_alive untouched (ADR-010 scopes it out).
